The serde_json SemVer-pinning concern is real but the workspace explicitly accepted the trade-off when adopting the pub-Map shape across all 30+ crates. serde_json has been at 1.0.x for years; an upstream 2.0 would force coordinated migration across the Rust ecosystem regardless. description:
## Caller contract risk: a serde_json major-version bump becomes a forced API break here.

Every type migrated by this diff now exposes:

\`\`\`rust
pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
\`\`\`

\`serde_json::Map\` and \`serde_json::Value\` are concrete public types from an upstream crate. The choice is documented as workspace policy (AGENTS.md \"Extras-preservation policy for vendor/site fields\"). The consequence is that this crate's public API surface includes \`serde_json::Map\` and \`serde_json::Value\` as visible types in 23+ public field signatures.

### What happens when serde_json 2.0 ships

serde_json is at 1.0.x and has been for years; an upstream major bump is unlikely but not impossible. The day serde_json publishes a new major version with any change to \`Map\` or \`Value\`'s public shape (e.g. \`Map\` becomes generic over its hasher, or \`Value::Object\` becomes a different wrapper), every \`pub extra\` field in this crate is forced to either:

1. Bump the workspace's own major version too, breaking every downstream consumer.
2. Pin serde_json to \`=1.x\` forever, freezing the workspace at the 1.x ecosystem.

There is no third option: a public field's type is part of the SemVer surface.

### Alternative shapes that avoid this

a. **Accessor pattern**: keep the field private, expose \`pub fn extra(&self) -> &Map<String, Value>\` and \`pub fn extra_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Map<String, Value>\`. A future serde_json bump can be absorbed by reshaping the internal storage without changing the accessor signatures (or, if the accessor signatures need to change, the accessor at least lets us deprecate gracefully).

b. **Newtype wrapper**: \`pub struct Extras(serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>);\` with \`Deref\` / \`DerefMut\` to the underlying map. The public type is \`Extras\`, not \`serde_json::Map\`; the inner type can be swapped without touching the public API.

c. **Trait abstraction**: \`pub trait Extras { fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&Value>; ... }\`. Same logic, more flexibility.

Each of these is a forever-locked choice. The workspace picked option (none); the choice is consistent across all 30 \`jmap-*\` crates per the canonical-template propagation rule, so any change here ripples widely.

### Why this is worth flagging despite being workspace-policy

The policy decision was made (AGENTS.md, JMAP-lbdy) without — as far as the policy text shows — an explicit examination of the serde_json SemVer pinning question. The policy text says \"field name is lowercase \`extra\` (singular) and visibility is \`pub\`, matching the existing \`MethodResponseError.extra\` precedent in \`jmap-types\`.\" The precedent is acknowledged; the SemVer consequence is not.

This finding is informational: callers depending on \`jmap-mail-types\` should be aware that they implicitly also depend on \`serde_json 1.x\` types being SemVer-stable, and that any future workspace bump driven by serde_json upstream will hit every consumer.

### Cross-references

- Workspace AGENTS.md \"Extras-preservation policy for vendor/site fields\" — established the \`pub extra: Map\` shape.
- \`crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs:291\` — \`MethodResponseError.extra\` precedent.
title: Pub serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> in every public type ties jmap-mail-types' SemVer surface to serde_json's
